title: Mutable default argument
code:
def add(item, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket

add(1)
add(2)
print(add(3))
question: What does this print?
explanation: The default list is created once, when the function is defined, and shared by every call that omits bucket. Use bucket=None and create the list inside.
model: It appends to one shared default list, so state leaks between calls; the third call sees the two earlier items.

title: Closures capture variables, not values
code:
fs = [lambda: i * i for i in range(4)]
print([f() for f in fs])
question: What does this print?
explanation: Each lambda looks up i when it is called; by then the comprehension has finished with i = 3. Bind the value with lambda i=i: i * i.
model: Builds four functions that all read the same loop variable late, so they all return 3 squared.

title: What does this function compute?
question: Given a sorted list a, what does mystery(a, x) return?
options: The first index whose value is ≥ x (bisect_left)
The first index whose value is > x (bisect_right)
The number of elements smaller than x
explanation: Every element ≤ x pushes lo to the right, so lo stops at the first element strictly greater than x — the same as bisect.bisect_right. It also equals the count of elements ≤ x.
model: Binary search for the insertion point after any existing copies of x: the number of elements ≤ x, i.e. bisect_right. O(log n).

title: Hidden quadratic
question: With n words of bounded length, what is the worst-case time complexity?
explanation: Each iteration splits the whole string built so far (O(n) work) and scans the resulting list (O(n)), so n iterations cost O(n²). A set of seen words plus ','.join makes it O(n).
model: Deduplicates words into a comma-separated string, but re-splits the growing string each time, so it is quadratic.

title: Find the bug: sliding window
question: longest_unique("abba") should be 2. Which line is wrong?
explanation: When the last 'a' is seen, its previous index 0 lies before the window start (2); setting start = 1 moves the window backwards and the function returns 3. Use start = max(start, seen[ch] + 1).
model: Longest substring without repeating characters with a last-seen map; the start pointer must never move left.

title: Generator laziness
code:
def gen():
    print("start")
    yield 1
    print("middle")
    yield 2

g = gen()
print("created")
print(next(g))
question: What does this print?
explanation: Calling a generator function only creates the generator; its body runs up to the first yield when next is called.
model: Shows that generator bodies run lazily, one yield at a time.

title: What does this function compute?
question: For a non-negative integer n, f(n) returns…
options: The number of 1 bits in n
explanation: n & (n − 1) clears the lowest set bit, so the loop runs once per 1 bit (Kernighan's popcount) — O(number of set bits).
model: Counts set bits by repeatedly clearing the lowest one.

title: Recursion depth and cost
question: Time complexity for a list of length n?
explanation: Each level of recursion copies O(n) elements in slices and concatenations, and there are log n levels: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) = O(n log n). It returns a copy of the list.
model: Splits the list in halves recursively and glues it back together — merge-sort shape without the sorting, so O(n log n) from copying.

title: Find the bug: BFS on a grid
question: It returns correct answers but is very slow on large open grids. Which line causes it?
explanation: Cells are marked visited when popped, so the same cell can be enqueued many times before it is processed — exponential-looking blow-up on open grids. Mark seen when you enqueue (and add start initially).
model: Shortest path in an unweighted grid with BFS; correctness holds but duplicates explode the queue.

title: What does this class do?
question: What data structure does S implement, and what is the cost of pop?
explanation: Two stacks reverse the order once: elements leave in insertion order (FIFO). Each element moves from a to b at most once, so pops are O(1) amortised (#232).
model: A FIFO queue built from two stacks; the transfer happens only when the out-stack is empty.

title: Memoised recursion
question: Time complexity of ways(m, n) with the cache?
explanation: There are (m+1)(n+1) distinct (i, j) states, each computed once with O(1) work. Without the cache it would be exponential.

title: Find the bug: heap of tuples
